questions.prompt: Food selection is only about what you buy at the shop

block.label: Swipe Sort
block.sub: Flick each card up into its bucket

questions.why: False — food selection also includes WHY we choose foods: taste, cost, culture, religion, and health all shape our choices, not just the shopping trip.

questions.subject: Food Technology
questions.prompt: Vitamins and minerals are only needed in tiny amounts

block.label: Swipe Sort
block.sub: Flick each card up into its bucket

questions.why: True — vitamins and minerals are needed only in small amounts, but they're still essential for the body to work properly, unlike the misconception that small amounts mean they don't matter.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 16 cm and a height of 5 cm. Work through it calmly — what is its area?
questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 16 × 5 = 40 cm². Say the ½ step out loud before multiplying to stop the rushing slip.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: If 33g of reactants react completely in a sealed container, what is the mass of the products?
questions.why: Mass is conserved in a closed system, so the products weigh exactly the same as the reactants: 33g.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What do we call the new substances left over after a chemical reaction finishes?
questions.why: The substances formed at the end of a reaction are called the products — made from the atoms of the original reactants rearranged into new bonds.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: A cereal ad uses a cartoon mascot and bright colours aimed at kids. What is this marketing technique mainly trying to do?
questions.why: Mascots and bright colours are designed to appeal directly to children, making the product feel fun and exciting so kids ask parents to buy it — not to inform about health or price.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: On a nutrition label, which nutrient usually gives the body the most energy per gram?
questions.why: Fat provides about 9 calories per gram, almost double carbohydrate or protein (about 4 each), so it packs the most energy per gram, a common mix-up on labels.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What do we call the substances you start with before a chemical reaction takes place?
questions.why: The starting substances in a chemical reaction are called the reactants — they are used up and rearranged to form the products.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: Which of these best describes a healthy food choice?
questions.why: A healthy choice balances foods from all groups in sensible amounts — cutting out whole groups (like all fat) or relying only on taste misses that balance is the key factor.

questions.subject: Food Technology
questions.prompt: A friend says 'food selection' just means choosing what to buy at the shop. Explain what's missing from this idea, and name at least two other real factors that shape what people actually eat.
